on terminal value risk -- obvious q would be, "how do Buffett/Munger think about situations like this?"

the answer is that they don't

just immediately gets tossed into the "too hard" pile along with prob 99.9% of the shit that comes across their desk

there's a bunch of quotes in here from them on discounting cash flows, opportunity cost, how they think about hurdle rates, but what needs to be understood is that BEFORE any of that even begins...there's the binary filter:

"do I have confidence/certainty in cash flows...CAP duration...predictable demand" etc

if it fails that qualitative test, the research process ends.

worth thinking about next time u wander into some big-brain debate on 2036 software fcf
